passage.text: A job interview is a great opportunity to show an employer what you can do.
passage.reading: ə ˈdʒɑːb ˈɪntərvjuː ɪz ə ˈɡreɪt ˌɑːpərˈtuːnəti tə ˈʃoʊ ən ɪmˈplɔɪər ˈwʌt juː kən ˈduː.

passage.text: But many candidates make the same mistakes again and again.
passage.reading: bʌt ˈmɛni ˈkændɪdəts ˈmeɪk ðə ˈseɪm mɪˈsteɪks əˈɡɛn ənd əˈɡɛn.

passage.text: Here are ten of the most common ones.
passage.reading: ˈhɪr ər ˈtɛn əv ðə ˈmoʊst ˈkɑːmən ˈwʌnz.

passage.text: The first mistake is arriving late, so leave home early.
passage.reading: ðə ˈfɜːrst mɪˈsteɪk ɪz əˈraɪvɪŋ ˈleɪt, soʊ ˈliːv ˈhoʊm ˈɜːrli.

passage.text: The second is not knowing anything about the company, so read its website before you go.
passage.reading: ðə ˈsɛkənd ɪz ˈnɑːt ˈnoʊɪŋ ˈɛniθɪŋ əˈbaʊt ðə ˈkʌmpəni, soʊ ˈriːd ɪts ˈwɛbsaɪt bɪˈfɔːr juː ˈɡoʊ.

passage.text: Third, some candidates do not dress smartly enough.
passage.reading: ˈθɜːrd, sʌm ˈkændɪdəts duː ˈnɑːt ˈdrɛs ˈsmɑːrtli ɪˈnʌf.

passage.text: Fourth, a weak handshake can make you look nervous, so shake hands with confidence.
passage.reading: ˈfɔːrθ, ə ˈwiːk ˈhændʃeɪk kən ˈmeɪk juː ˈlʊk ˈnɜːrvəs, soʊ ˈʃeɪk ˈhændz wɪð ˈkɑːnfɪdəns.

passage.text: Your body language is important, too.
passage.reading: jʊr ˈbɑːdi ˌlæŋɡwɪdʒ ɪz ɪmˈpɔːrtənt, ˈtuː.

passage.text: Sitting with your arms crossed and checking your phone are mistakes five and six.
passage.reading: ˈsɪtɪŋ wɪð jʊr ˈɑːrmz ˈkrɔːst ənd ˈtʃɛkɪŋ jʊr ˈfoʊn ər mɪˈsteɪks ˈfaɪv ənd ˈsɪks.

passage.text: Mistake number seven is talking too much, so keep your answers short and clear.
passage.reading: mɪˈsteɪk ˈnʌmbər ˈsɛvən ɪz ˈtɔːkɪŋ ˈtuː ˈmʌtʃ, soʊ ˈkiːp jʊr ˈænsərz ˈʃɔːrt ənd ˈklɪr.

passage.text: Many interviewers ask, "What is your greatest weakness?"
passage.reading: ˈmɛni ˈɪntərvjuːərz ˈæsk, ˈwʌt ɪz jʊr ˈɡreɪtɪst ˈwiːknəs?

passage.text: Saying "I don't have any weaknesses" is mistake number eight.
passage.reading: ˈseɪɪŋ aɪ ˈdoʊnt ˈhæv ˈɛni ˈwiːknəsɪz ɪz mɪˈsteɪk ˈnʌmbər ˈeɪt.

passage.text: Instead, choose a real weakness and explain how you are improving it.
passage.reading: ɪnˈstɛd, ˈtʃuːz ə ˈriːəl ˈwiːknəs ənd ɪkˈspleɪn ˈhaʊ juː ər ɪmˈpruːvɪŋ ɪt.

passage.text: When you talk about your strengths, give examples from your studies or your work.
passage.reading: wɛn juː ˈtɔːk əˈbaʊt jʊr ˈstrɛŋθs, ˈɡɪv ɪɡˈzæmpəlz frəm jʊr ˈstʌdiz ɔːr jʊr ˈwɜːrk.

passage.text: Mistake number nine is saying bad things about your old boss.
passage.reading: mɪˈsteɪk ˈnʌmbər ˈnaɪn ɪz ˈseɪɪŋ ˈbæd ˈθɪŋz əˈbaʊt jʊr ˈoʊld ˈbɔːs.

passage.text: Finally, many candidates forget to ask questions at the end.
passage.reading: ˈfaɪnəli, ˈmɛni ˈkændɪdəts fərˈɡɛt tu ˈæsk ˈkwɛstʃənz ət ði ˈɛnd.

passage.text: That is mistake number ten, because interviewers want to see that you are really interested in the job.
passage.reading: ðæt ɪz mɪˈsteɪk ˈnʌmbər ˈtɛn, bɪˈkɔːz ˈɪntərvjuːərz ˈwɑːnt tə ˈsiː ðæt juː ər ˈriːli ˈɪntrəstɪd ɪn ðə ˈdʒɑːb.

passage.text: Avoid these ten mistakes, and your next interview will go much better.
passage.reading: əˈvɔɪd ðiːz ˈtɛn mɪˈsteɪks, ənd jʊr ˈnɛkst ˈɪntərvjuː wɪl ˈɡoʊ ˈmʌtʃ ˈbɛtər.
